title: 08 · Design with level data
language: English / Thai guidance · English Python identifiers
assumptions: New proposed course for the C2–C3 readiness range, not an approved replacement for Creator 2 or Creator 3.
Provisional pre-lesson 90 minutes + 10 × 90 minutes; 8 learners, one computer per learner or rotating pairs. Ages 10–15 are a design assumption; placement uses readiness.
Desktop Python required. First install needs internet; classroom OS and editor must be checked by the teacher.
Generated assets and support code are supplied resources, not evidence of student authorship.

objectives.statement: Explain and predict: A dictionary separates level content from shared rules
objectives.evidence: After a player removes a target then presses R, why should all targets return? Point to the copy that protects the template.

objectives.statement: Design and test a meaningful change to this mechanic.
objectives.evidence: Add a third level through data only. Make a meaningful contrast in route choice, not just more obstacles.

prerequisites: Retrieve lists and reset. Bridge a dictionary key such as targets to its value before indexing levels[level].
entry_check: Retrieve lists and reset. Bridge a dictionary key such as targets to its value before indexing levels[level]. If the trace needs heavy prompting, spend the first 8 minutes on the bridge and use the support route.
materials: Tested desktop Python 3.12 + pygame-ce 2.5.8; keyboard; offline extracted student ZIP.
Projector, paper coordinate frame / trace sheet, and the supplied PNG assets.
prep: Extract the full student package and follow the setup file on a classroom machine.
Run the teacher reference.py, verify the predicted result and test teacher_example.py separately. Student starter.py intentionally contains TODOs.
Keep teacher notes and answer keys out of projection. Display the actual Python window during Run.
Print the trace/playtest worksheet. Prepare an offline paper fallback and assign rotating pair roles.

differentiation.support: Provide a key/value diagram and edit one coordinate pair at a time.
differentiation.core: Change only level 2 obstacle positions to (400,260) and (580,400). Verify both levels and restart.
differentiation.stretch: Validate a level for unreachable goals or overlapping starts; explain what automatic checks cannot judge about fun.
differentiation.access: Accept Thai oral explanations or a paper trace. Enlarge code and reduce typing with the starter. Use untimed practice and a no-flash option. Distinguish keyboard difficulty from understanding.
differentiation.late_arrival: Use the supplied starter checkpoint; trace one rule with the navigator, then take a driver turn and an individual exit check.
differentiation.short_route: 60-minute route: setup 5, Predict 5, Run 5, Investigate 10, Modify 12, Make 15, Grow 8. Keep one design choice and the individual check; defer extra polish.
differentiation.fallback: Act as the computer using the exact starter code, paper variables and sprite cards. Predict and trace the same state changes. This checks reasoning but does not verify graphics, keyboard control or installation.

resources.title: Setup and run instructions
resources.content:
GAME DESIGNER · desktop Python starter
Use Python 3.12 and pygame-ce 2.5.8 (the development test environment).
Teacher: install and test on every classroom OS before class. Other Python versions are unverified.

Extract the WHOLE ZIP. Keep starter.py, studio.py, images/ and fonts/ together.
Open a terminal in the extracted folder.
Windows: py -3.12 -m venv .venv
macOS/Linux: python3.12 -m venv .venv
Windows install: .venv\Scripts\python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
macOS/Linux install: .venv/bin/python -m pip install -r requirements.txt
Windows run: .venv\Scripts\python starter.py
macOS/Linux run: .venv/bin/python starter.py

Initial installation needs internet and permission to install packages. Afterwards games run locally without accounts or internet. A Chromebook/browser-only device is not an assumed supported setup.
Keep a tested copy of each lesson for catch-up. Do not name your file pygame.py.

Controls: arrows move from lesson 2; R resets from lesson 4; Esc or close quits.
Hold H to show the player's 48×48 hitbox. Artwork is scaled at runtime; source PNGs are unchanged.
Lesson 1 is a static scene. Lessons 1–3 restart by closing and running again.
Each lesson is a separate concept checkpoint, not a promise that every earlier mechanic is carried forward.
Lessons 6–10 omit the countdown; lesson 8 onward omit the patrol to isolate data and design.

studio.py is teacher-provided infrastructure. It owns window/events, dt, graphics, font loading and a simple touching helper. Read it when ready; it is not learner-authored evidence. Students edit starter.py. Pre-lesson 00 introduces simple classes and independent objects. The graphical lessons use functions; inheritance, a physics engine and Unity syntax are not required.
Game UI and code identifiers use English; teacher guidance is bilingual. Accept Thai explanations.
